en: Hello, dispatch {tr_id} of {tonnes} tonnes on {date} names lot {lot}, but the trace check shows: {state}. Please find the lot record or the harvest sheet today, because the buyer asks for it.
Hello, we send {tonnes} tonnes of {crop} from lot {lot} on {date}. It was harvested on {harvest_date} on {field}. Delivery note {note_no}, truck {truck}. We can send the analysis on request.
Hello, we received your complaint {cq_id} about lot {lot} ({product}, {cause}). We will check our records and the kept sample and answer you soon. Thank you for telling us.
Hello, we sent a sample of lot {lot} ({crop}) for testing. Please send your own result for the delivery of {date} so that we can compare the two and keep our records complete.
Hello, pickup {del_id} on {date}: {litres} litres, fat {fat}, protein {protein}, cell count {scc}. The result is: {result}. Please confirm that this matches your test.
Buyer: pickup window for the lot
Hello, lot {lot} ({crop}, {tonnes} tonnes) is ready for pickup around {date}. Please tell us your truck and the day you plan to collect.
Hello, please service our grain dryer before the harvest. The last job was on {date} for lot {lot}, {hours} hours of work. Tell us your first free day and your price.
Contractor: pest control in the store
Hello, please visit the farm to treat {name} ({kind}) for pests before we fill it again. The last clean-down was on {last_clean}. Tell us your first free day.
Hello, we need {missing} more {kind}. Buyers still hold crates from our dispatch {cr_id}. Please send your price and the first delivery date.
Hello, the fan of {name} needs repair before the next filling. The bin holds {content_t} tonnes of {product}. Please send a technician and a price.
Staff: egg packing team for tomorrow
Hello {packer}, tomorrow the team packs {eggs_in} {grade} eggs for {buyer}. Please prepare the trays, the date stamps and the cartons.
Hello, batch {batch} of {animals} animals ({herd}) goes on {date}. Please record the live weights before loading and the carcass weights at the abattoir and send them to me.
Staff: wool clip bagged and labelled
Hello, the {grade} wool from {herd} ({fleece_kg} kg, clip of {date}) must be bagged and labelled. {shearer} will help. Please keep the bags dry in the flat store.
Hello {counter}, the store count of {product} is planned for {date}. Please prepare the sheet, close the movements the evening before and bring the stock card.
Hello, the labels for lot {lot_id} ({crop}, {field}, {tonnes} tonnes, harvested {date}) are printed. Please fix a label on every bag or crate and one on the store card.

We produced {col:unitcost.produced} {col:unitcost.unit} this year. The total cost was {col:unitcost.total}, of which direct costs were {col:unitcost.direct}, labour {col:unitcost.labour}, storage and drying {col:unitcost.storage}, packaging {col:unitcost.packaging} and other costs {col:unitcost.other}.

The cost of one unit is {col:unitcost.cost_unit} and the price is {col:unitcost.price_unit}, so the margin is {col:unitcost.margin_unit} for each unit ({col:unitcost.margin_pct} of the price). The margin check shows: {col:unitcost.state}.
We read this report every month with the stock and loss records before we decide what to store, sell or change.
Dispatch {col:trace.tr_id} to {col:trace.buyer} on {col:trace.date}. Delivery note {col:trace.note_no}, truck {col:trace.truck}.

The goods are {col:trace.tonnes} tonnes of {col:trace.crop} from lot {col:trace.lot}. The lot was harvested on {col:trace.harvest_date} on the field {col:trace.field} and was kept in store for {col:trace.days_stored} days before this dispatch.
Our trace check shows: {col:trace.state}. The harvest sheet, the moisture result and the store records for this lot are kept on the farm and can be shown on request.
We confirm that the details above come from our own farm records.
Milk quality statement for a pickup

The load was {col:mdeliv.litres} litres with fat {col:mdeliv.fat}, protein {col:mdeliv.protein}, a cell count of {col:mdeliv.scc} thousand per ml and a bacteria count of {col:mdeliv.bact} thousand per ml.

The test result is: {col:mdeliv.result}. We are paid for {col:mdeliv.pay_l} litres at {col:mdeliv.price_l} per litre, which is {col:mdeliv.value}. Our own limits are a cell count of {set:scc_limit} and bacteria of {set:bact_limit}.
Please send us your laboratory report if it differs from this statement.
Egg production report for a collection

There were {col:eggs.hens} hens in lay and we collected {col:eggs.eggs} eggs, which is a hen-day lay rate of {col:eggs.lay_rate}. {col:eggs.cracked} eggs were cracked ({col:eggs.crack_pct}), so {col:eggs.good} eggs were good.
Our targets are a lay rate of {set:lay_target} and cracked eggs below {set:crack_limit}. The check shows: {col:eggs.state}.
The keeper looks at feed, water, light and handling whenever the check is not on target.
Stock list of a bin or silo
It holds {col:bins.content_t} tonnes of {col:bins.product} out of {col:bins.capacity_t} tonnes of capacity. The fill is {col:bins.pct_full} and the space left is {col:bins.space_t} tonnes.

The moisture is {col:bins.moisture} and the moisture check shows: {col:bins.moist_state}. The last inspection was on {col:bins.last_inspect} and the check shows: {col:bins.insp_state}. The value of the content is {col:bins.value}.
The keeper signs this list after counting the store.
We lost {col:loss.tonnes} tonnes of {col:loss.product} from lot {col:loss.lot}. The cause is {col:loss.cause}. The value lost is {col:loss.value} and the size of the loss is {col:loss.size}.
The affected stock was separated, the area was cleaned and the cause was written in the store record. Our accepted storage loss is {set:loss_limit} of the stock.
The report goes to the farm manager and to the insurer when the loss is large.
Product: {col:pack.product}, quality {col:pack.pclass}. We packed {col:pack.crates} crates of {col:pack.crate_kg} kilograms, which is {col:pack.net_kg} kilograms net or {col:pack.tonnes} tonnes.
We took out {col:pack.rejected_kg} kilograms as rejects ({col:pack.reject_pct}). The value of the load is {col:pack.value}. The packing check shows: {col:pack.state}.
Please count the crates when they arrive and return the empty crates and pallets in good order.

Thank you for telling us about the problem: {col:complaint.cause}, {col:complaint.qty_t} tonnes affected. Your claim is {col:complaint.claim}, which is {col:complaint.claim_pct} of the value of those goods.
We checked the lot records, the moisture result and the store notes for this lot. The complaint has been open for {col:complaint.days_open} days and is handled by {col:complaint.handled_by}.
We will agree the credit or the replacement with you and we will write down what we change so that it does not happen again.
We counted {col:count.counted_t} tonnes. The book stock from the movements is {col:count.book_t} tonnes, so the difference is {col:count.diff_t} tonnes ({col:count.diff_pct}).
The book value is {col:count.book_value} and the value of the difference is {col:count.diff_value}. The count check shows: {col:count.state}. We accept a difference of {set:count_tol}.
A difference above the limit is counted again and explained in the movement records before the book is corrected.

Open Start and type your farm name and your own limits in the yellow cells: cell count, fat, tank temperature, lay rate, moisture, humidity, loss and count tolerance.
Fill Grades and Prices first: one row for each product and quality class with the price per tonne. Stock values, losses and complaints use these prices.
Enter every milking on Milk Records and every pickup on Milk Deliveries. The quality check and the paid litres fill in.
Enter each egg collection on Egg Collection and the weekly grading and packing on Egg Grading.
Record slaughter batches on Meat Records and each clip on Wool Clips.
Give every load a number on Harvest Lots. Moisture, tonnes sent and the link to a buyer fill in as you record dispatches.
Describe each bin and silo on Bins and Silos and each cold room, store or tank on Cold Rooms with the temperature range it must hold.
Record every tonne in, out and corrected on Stock Movements. Count the stock on Stock Counts and read the difference against the book.
Log drying jobs on Drying and Cleaning, temperatures on Temperature Log, losses on Storage Losses and packing runs on Packing and Grading.
Record each dispatch on Lot Traceability with the lot number. The field, crop and harvest date fill in and a check shows any gap.
Track crates on Crates and Pallets, complaints on Quality Complaints and the cost of every product on Cost per Unit.

Use the 13 calculators for bin size, drying shrink, drying cost, milk per cow, feed per litre, lay rate, cost per dozen, dressing, days of stock, loss, lot lookup, crates and the store or sell decision.
Read Production Dashboard and Charts every week: milk, eggs, stock, cold chain, losses, traceability and complaints.
Run machines, fuel and seasonal labour with costs and warnings
Machines, fuel, seasonal workers, pay and safety in one file
hours since the last service come straight from the hours log, with hours left, the expected date and a warning before and after the limit
Cost per hour of every machine
depreciation, repairs and fuel of the last 12 months divided by the hours worked give a true cost per hour for each machine
Fuel per hectare and per task
litres per hour and per hectare for every job, with a warning when a job burns more than the usual use of the machine
every dip is compared with purchases less use, so a loss or a low stock shows before the tank runs dry
Breakdowns with cost of lost days
days down and the day rate of the machine give the cost of each breakdown, and the register shows which machines are down now
hire invoices are compared with what an own machine would cost, and a calculator finds the break-even hours per year
Piece-rate pay with minimum pay top-up
kilograms, rejects and rate give the pay, the kilograms per hour and any top-up needed to reach the lowest hourly pay
hours against the contract show overtime and its pay, and months with too few rest days or too much overtime are flagged
pesticide, tractor, first aid and other certificates show days left and who must renew before they can work
labour hours needed each month are turned into workers and compared with the contracts you have, so the shortage is known weeks early
permanent, seasonal and piece-rate pay with employer costs are added up every month and compared with your labour budget and cost per hectare
Safety log with days without an incident
incidents, near misses and protective equipment issued are kept together, with open actions and the days since the last incident

Machines register: the fleet, its cost and age
One row for each machine, owned or hired, with price, life and day rate; age, value, hours, repair and fuel cost, cost per hour and the service and age checks fill in by themselves.
Machine hours log: machine, task, field and hours
One row for each job with machine, attachment, field, task, operator, hours and hectares; the cost of the job, hectares per hour and the operator phone fill in by themselves.
Service schedule: hours since each service and hours left
One row for each machine and kind of service with the interval in hours and the date of the last service; hours since, hours left, expected date and a due warning fill in from the hours log.
Repair log: what broke, who repaired it and what it cost
One row for each repair with the part group, parts cost, workshop hours and the date it was finished; labour cost, total cost, days open and a long-repair warning fill in.
Breakdowns and downtime: days lost and what they cost
One row for each breakdown with the cause, the field where it happened and the day the machine worked again; days down, the cost of the lost days and whether it is still down fill in.
Fuel purchases: deliveries, prices and payment
One row for each delivery of diesel, petrol or oil with litres, price, supplier and payment terms; cost, the day payment is due and a payment check fill in.
Fuel use per task and field
One row for each job with litres used, hours and hectares worked; litres per hour and per hectare, the cost and a check against the usual use of the machine fill in.
Fuel tank dips: measured stock against the books
One row for each dip of the diesel tank with the litres measured; the stock the books expect, the difference, days of cover and a loss or low-stock warning fill in from purchases and use.
Implements and attachments: work rate, hours and condition
One row for each attachment with width, speed and the share of time it really works; hectares per hour, hours and hectares in 12 months and a condition check fill in from the hours log.
Workshop spare parts stock and what to reorder
One row for each part with the stock, the least you want to hold and the unit cost; stock value, quantity to order, order cost and a reorder warning fill in.
Contract machinery hire: what it costs against owning
One row for each hire with contractor, dates, hours and price per hour; days, cost, what an own machine would cost and the saving or loss from hiring fill in.
Permanent staff: roles, cost per hour and certificate check
One row for each permanent staff member with role, cost per hour and contract hours; monthly pay, employer costs, hours this month, overtime and the certificate check fill in.
Seasonal and casual workers: contracts, hours and pay
One row for each seasonal or casual worker with the contract dates and pay per hour; contract days, hours, pay by the hour, piece-rate kilograms and pay and the contract status fill in.
Timesheets: hours worked every day and what they cost
One row for each worker and day with field, task and hours; the pay rate, overtime hours, pay and the cost with employer costs fill in.
Piece-rate picking: kilograms, rejects and pay
One row for each picker and day with kilograms picked and rejected, rate and hours; net kilograms, pay, kilograms per hour and the top-up to the lowest hourly pay fill in.
Overtime and rest days of the permanent staff by month
One row for each person and month with the hours worked and the rest days taken; contract hours, overtime, pay and a warning for missing rest days or too much overtime fill in.
Training and certificates: who holds what and when it ends
One row for each certificate with the date issued and how long it lasts; the end date, days left and a valid, ending soon or expired check fill in.
Safety log: incidents, near misses and equipment
One row for each incident, near miss or issue of protective equipment with the person, field, cost and the day it was closed; incident flag, age and an action check fill in.
What happened or what was issued
Payroll summary by month: pay, employer costs and budget
One row for each month with your budget and allowances; pay of staff, seasonal workers and pickers, employer costs, labour cost and the gap to budget fill in.
Labour need by month against workers available
One row for each month with the labour hours the farm work needs and the permanent staff; workers needed, seasonal workers on contract, the gap and a shortage warning fill in.

Hello {mechanic}, {machine} needs its {svc} in {left} hours (interval {interval_h} hours, last service on {last_date}). Please book the workshop and order the parts.
Hello {mechanic}, the pre-harvest checks start soon. Please check {machine} on {planned_on} ({svc}) and tell me what must be repaired before the harvest.
Hello {mechanic}, {machine} broke down on {date} in {field}: {note}. It has been down for {days_down} days. Please come today and tell me what it needs.
Hello {repairer}, the spare part for {machine} ({repair}) is ordered. Please tell me when you can fit it. We would like the machine ready by {est_ready}.
Hello {repairer}, we need {machine} back by {est_ready}. It has been open for {days_open} days. Please tell me what is still missing.
Hello {repairer}, please send the cost estimate for {repair} on {machine} before you start. The parts so far are {parts_cost} and the workshop time is {labour_h} hours.
Hello {repairer}, we need a visit to repair {machine} ({part}). Please tell me your first free day and the price per hour for the repair on the farm.
Hello {repairer}, your invoice for {repair} on {machine} must match the repair order of {cost}. Parts {parts_cost} and {labour_h} hours. Please send a corrected invoice if it differs.
Hello {operator}, please confirm the hours of {machine} for {date}: {hours} hours. If the number is not right, send me the correct hours and the field today.
Hello {dip_by}, the diesel tank held {measured} litres on {date}, which is {days_cover} days of cover. Please dip the tank again tomorrow and tell me the litres.
Hello {keeper}, please look at {name} behind {pulled_by}. Its condition is marked {cond} and the last check was on {last_check}. Tell me what is damaged and take a photo.
Hello, please deliver {litres} litres of {product} on the agreed day. The last price was {price_l} per litre. Payment is due {terms_days} days after delivery.
Hello, please send {to_order} pieces of {part} for {machine}. We have {qty} in stock and need at least {min_qty}. Please tell me the price and the delivery date.
Hello, we confirm the order of {part} for {machine}. Please deliver within {lead_days} days with the delivery note and the price of {unit_cost} each.
Hello {contractor}, we book {machine} from {start_date} to {end_date} for {field}, about {hours} hours at {rate_h} per hour. Please confirm the crew and the arrival time.
Hello {contractor}, the harvest on {field} starts on {start_date}. Please send {machine} with the crew and tell me the time of arrival, the width and the fuel you need on the farm.
Hello {contractor}, please send the work record for {machine} on {field}: hours, hectares and any waiting time. We compare it with our log of about {hours} hours.
Hello {name}, the shift starts at 6:00 tomorrow. Please come in your protective clothing and check the work list with your supervisor first.
Hello {name}, please hand in your timesheet for this week by Friday. This month you have {hours_month} hours on record. Please tell me about any overtime or day off.
Hello {staff}, your overtime for {month} is approved: {ot_hours} hours. Please also take your rest days, you have taken {rest_days} so far.
Hello {staff}, your pay slip for {month} is ready. You worked {hours} hours and the pay is {pay}. Please tell the office if anything looks wrong.
Hello {staff}, your next course for {cert} is on {course_on} with {provider}. Please keep the day free and tell me if you cannot come.
Hello {staff}, your {cert} certificate ends on {expires}, in {days_left} days. Please book the renewal course now, because you cannot do this work without it.
Seasonal worker: start date and place
Hello {name}, welcome to the farm. Your work starts on {start_date}. Please come to the main gate at 6:00 and ask for {leader}. Bring your identity document and work boots.
Hello {name}, the farm bus leaves the housing at 6:30 tomorrow for the field. Your task is {main_task} and your team leader is {leader}. Please be ready 10 minutes early.
Seasonal worker: rate and pay day

Hello {name}, your pay is {rate_h} per hour. Piece work is paid by the kilogram and never below {rate_h} per hour for the hours worked. Pay day is every second Friday. Your total so far is {total_pay}.
Hello {name}, thank you for your work from {start_date} to {end_date}. We would like you back next season at the same rate or better. Please tell me if you are free.
Hello {manager}, in {month} we need {seasonal_needed} seasonal workers and have {seasonal_hired} on contract, so {gap} workers are short. Please start hiring now.
Farm manager: labour cost this month
Hello {manager}, the labour cost for {month} is {labour_cost} against a budget of {budget}. Budget left: {variance}. Please check the overtime and the piece-rate pay.
